manifest.name: recx
manifest.summary: A manifest format that lets coding agents find and reuse other people's open-source work.
manifest.description:
res extra commercium: things outside commerce. A repository drops RECX.yaml at
its root to say what it does, which of its modules can be taken on their own,
how to take them, and which checks anyone can rerun to see that they work.
GitHub code search on the filename is the index, so there is no service to
run. This repository holds the spec, and it is the spec's first adopter.
capabilities: define a manifest format describing a repository's reusable modules to coding agents
validate a RECX.yaml manifest with any JSON Schema 2020-12 validator
keep a repository's RECX.yaml valid as a Claude Code session ends

modules.summary: The JSON Schema that defines a valid RECX.yaml.

extract.notes: The schema is one self-contained file, so copying spec/recx.schema.json works too. In Python it ships inside recx-cli.

modules.summary: Valid and invalid example manifests for testing any recx validator.

entrypoints: spec/examples/invalid/*.yaml: every file must be rejected, for the reason its first-line comment names
spec/examples/invalid-rules/*.yaml: every file passes the schema alone but must be rejected by the rules beyond it (recx check --no-repo)

modules.summary: The recx check command, which validates a RECX.yaml against the schema and the rules beyond it.
The Claude Code plugin, with the recx:manifest skill and a Stop hook that keeps RECX.yaml valid.

extract.notes: Installing through the marketplace is the intended route; copying plugin/ works but the hook then needs recx-cli 0.0.2 or later.

modules.summary: A composite GitHub Action that runs recx check, and optionally recx evidence, in a repository's CI.

extract.notes: Referencing it with "uses:" in a workflow is the intended route; copying action.yml works but it then installs recx-cli from PyPI like any user.
